learning: No race telemetry yet for this geometry. The next race should show whether the forward look-ahead cuts max_error and line losses without raising steering_oscillation, and whether kd 0.5 is enough damping.
notes: Complete runnable robot for the Builder's forward-sensor, 16 mm footprint geometry on the iteration 1 drivetrain. Only the sensor geometry changes from iteration 1; kd rises from 0.4 to 0.5 to damp the extra phase lead from the forward sensors.
rationale: Iteration 1 showed that spread alone did not reduce line losses (1.05 to 1.1 per run, against 1.0 to 1.35 before) and lowered oval progress from 0.72 to 0.62, so the limit is probably reaction lag rather than blindness. This iteration keeps the Builder's iteration 1 drivetrain (track 0.10 m, radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg) and changes only the sensors: forward to y=0.07 m, and footprint 16 mm, so the sensors see about 0.07 m further ahead of the axle. Sensor weights stay at [-2,-1,0,1,2], matching the iteration 1 spread of ±0.036 m. Forward sensors add phase lead, so the controller could overshoot. I therefore keep kp at 3.5 and raise kd from 0.4 to 0.5 to damp the earlier signal. The base speed stays at 1.6 and line_loss stays at last_direction, so the race isolates the sensor change. Expected result, untested: fewer line-loss events and a lower max_error than iteration 1 on s-bend and slalom, with oval progress recovering toward 0.72. Finishing on s-bend or slalom is still unlikely.
